clue.text: Go after Asian river business

blocks.note: the Indus is a great river of Pakistan and India
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to chase up an Asian river and make a business of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go after' tells you the word for go is placed after the river, so the river comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry is commerce or trade in general, and a business can be called an industry.

clue.text: Drink - one tipple brought in by me

indicators.note: something brought in by another is taken inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
to bib is an old verb meaning to drink habitually

explanation.surface: A host confesses to bringing in a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The tipple goes inside ME, and the numeral one stands in front of the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, especially alcohol, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: From a republic in Africa, a young man's turned up to see spiritual leader

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top, so the order flips

blocks.note: taken as written
Mali is a landlocked West African republic
taken as written
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A young man from an African country travels up to meet a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the chief spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Small lumberjack, one who toils

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a logger fells trees for timber

explanation.surface: A short woodcutter is described as a hard worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogger is a person who works doggedly and laboriously.

clue.text: Ornate orb connoisseur misrepresented in book

indicators.note: something ornate is elaborately worked over, suggesting letters rearranged into fancy patterns
a thing misrepresented is shown in a false form, so its letters are not in their true order

blocks.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An art expert's view of a decorated globe is misreported in print.
explanation.walkthrough: Ornate looks like part of the picture, describing the orb, but it reinforces the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is Daniel Defoe's 1719 novel of a castaway, so it is an example of a book.

clue.text: In Tolkien, Tom Bombadil's put six feet under . . .

indicators.note: the letters are found within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: sits across the end of the author's name, the forename and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: A Tolkien character, Tom Bombadil, is buried, with the ellipsis carrying on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Bombadil is an eccentric character in The Lord of the Rings; the ellipsis links this clue with 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Six feet under is the idiom for buried, and to entomb is to put a body in a tomb.

clue.text: Annoyed, wanted to catch learner driver

indicators.note: catching something means holding it, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: to want something can mean to need it
L is the learner plate on British cars

explanation.surface: Someone irritated is keen to catch a learner driver out.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle is to provoke or irritate, so needled means irked.

clue.text: Being broadcast from Barcelona, ironically

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words that follow

blocks.note: straddles the end of the city and the start of the adverb

explanation.surface: A programme is going out live from Barcelona, with a touch of irony.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is being transmitted live on radio or television.

clue.text: Past patron saint causes an exclamation

blocks.note: to go by is to go past
St George is the patron saint of England

explanation.surface: A saint from long ago makes someone cry out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild old-fashioned oath expressing surprise, so it is an example of an interjection.

clue.text: Legal walk

blocks.note: first meaning: in accordance with a constitution, lawful
second meaning: a stroll taken for the sake of one's health

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a phrase about a permitted stroll; they are separate senses of one word, one adjective and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what a constitution permits, and the noun is a regular health-giving stroll.

clue.text: . . . Baggins (hobbit) heartily upset about Bombadil's end

indicators.note: from the heart means only the inner letters are kept, the outer ones discarded
upset things are knocked about, so the letters land in a new order
going about something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another
the end of a name is its final letter alone

blocks.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: Continuing from 5 across, Baggins the hobbit is heartily upset about something to do with Bombadil.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged heart of the word hobbit is split around the final letter of Bombadil.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilbo Baggins is the hobbit hero of Tolkien's novel The Hobbit, so the surname identifies the character.

clue.text: Embargo on ballistic missile

indicators.note: going ballistic means flying into a wild rage, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A trade ban is imposed on a ballistic missile, an arms-control headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ballistic missile' reads as one phrase, but the adjective is the rearrangement signal and the noun alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomerang is a curved throwing weapon, so it is a kind of projectile.

clue.text: Produce item of jewellery found inside container

indicators.note: a thing found inside another is placed within it

blocks.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery
a bin is a receptacle

explanation.surface: A ring turns up inside a box and has to be produced.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in can mean to produce or yield, as of earnings or a harvest, or to introduce legislation.

clue.text: Battle of New Orleans?

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so the letters are remade in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It asks after the 1815 Battle of New Orleans in the American war against Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of New Orleans is a real battle, so the whole phrase seems a single name; New is the signal and Orleans the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno in Italy gave its name to the 1943 Allied landings and the fighting that followed, so it names a battle.

clue.text: About average on violin, having committed tune to memory originally

indicators.note: having something committed means having it put inside, as into custody
originally points to how a word begins, so only its first letter is kept

blocks.note: playing the violin is fiddling
an air is a melody
taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A violinist who has learnt a tune by heart turns out to be only middling.
explanation.walkthrough: The tune, to and the first letter of memory all go inside the playing, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair to middling is an informal phrase meaning moderately good, neither bad nor excellent.

clue.text: Train in club on piece of gymnastic equipment

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing on another is written above it

blocks.note: an iron is a golf club
the vaulting horse or pommel horse

explanation.surface: A gymnast trains with a club while on the apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' reads as a verb about practising, but it is the noun for a railway engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is an old, chiefly American nickname for a steam locomotive and so for a train.

clue.text: Watch tapes etc., haphazardly

indicators.note: done haphazardly means done without plan or order, so the letters fall randomly

blocks.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone watches video tapes and other things at random.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to look on as a member of an audience, so it is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: One altering certain features in a theatre?

definitions.text: One altering certain features in a theatre?

blocks.clueFragment: One altering certain features in a theatre?
blocks.note: surface reading: a stage make-up artist or set designer changing things in a playhouse
setter's reading: facial features reshaped in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A backstage worker reshapes parts of the stage set in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A theatre is also a hospital operating room, and features are the parts of a face.
explanation.definitionFit: This doctor reshapes noses, chins and other facial features by operating in a hospital.

clue.text: Article on more complex proposition that has been proved

indicators.note: something complex is intricate and tangled, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the definite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on a more complicated proposition that has been proved.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a statement that has been demonstrated by reasoning from axioms.

clue.text: Haughty and extremely excitable man of high rank abroad

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those letters are kept

blocks.note: grand can mean lofty or haughty in manner
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A haughty, highly strung nobleman abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for excitable; it takes only that word's two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank, hence abroad.

clue.text: Time off in bay

blocks.note: first meaning: a break from work, as in a parliamentary or school holiday
second meaning: an alcove or indentation in a wall

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a holiday spent by the sea, but bay here is the architectural alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is both an adjournment or break and a hollow set back into a wall.

clue.text: Hot drink required in not entirely warm French castle

indicators.note: something required in a place is needed inside it, so it goes within
not the whole thing means the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: chaud is French for warm
tea is a hot drink

explanation.surface: A hot drink is needed in a chilly French castle.
explanation.walkthrough: French does double work: it makes warm a French word, and the answer is itself the French word for castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a French castle or large country house.

clue.text: A long letter

blocks.note: taken as written
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: It seems to describe a lengthy letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective; it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the spelt-out name of the letter H.

clue.text: Terrible tsar stuck on promontory in novel

indicators.note: stuck on means attached alongside, so one piece is joined to the next

blocks.note: Ivan the Terrible was the first tsar of Russia
a hoe is a projecting ridge of land, as in Plymouth Hoe

explanation.surface: A cruel Russian ruler marooned on a headland in a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is Sir Walter Scott's 1819 historical novel, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: PM includes this one not far away

indicators.note: sent away means scattered from where it stood, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister includes someone who is close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem, Latin for after midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation p.m. covers the hours after midday, so that span of the day is within it.

clue.text: Group's leader brought in awful song

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is taken
bringing something in puts it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
dire means dreadful

explanation.surface: A band's frontman brings in a terrible number.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament for the dead, so it is a kind of tune.

clue.text: Former Scottish philosopher, the opposite of 5

blocks.note: ex means former
David Hume, the eighteenth-century Edinburgh philosopher

explanation.surface: A one-time Scottish thinker is the reverse of another answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig a buried body up, undoing what 5 across did.

clue.text: Knowing nothing, such a crossword can't be solved!

definitions.text: such a crossword can't be solved

blocks.note: first meaning: ignorant, without any idea

blocks.clueFragment: such a crossword can't be solved
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a grid lacking any hints

explanation.surface: Someone ignorant complains that a puzzle cannot be solved.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a playful literal reading of the word: without clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ignorant, and taken literally it means lacking hints.
